notes:
FAULT FIXED - YES, decisively, and measured rather than eyeballed. Attempt 1's featured pocket read 13.5 deg from HORIZONTAL (76.5 deg from vertical), i.e. near-horizontal. Attempt 2 reads 11.04-11.34 deg from VERTICAL. The mouth rotated ~65 deg and now lands within 0.8 deg of the drawing.

METHOD AND ITS VALIDATION. Sibling drawing 3122 carries a printed RED dimension callout over the pocket mouth - the one place in this family where the drawing tells you which line is the feature. Fitting the red pixels alone gives 22.96 deg from vertical. Running my blind ink-tracer on the same drawing gives 22.92 deg. A 0.04 deg agreement, so the tracer is measuring the feature it names. Applied to all four family drawings (deg from vertical): 3100 (2.0 cm) 8.63, 3104 (2.5 cm) 11.88, 3101 (3.2 cm) 12.55, 3122 (5.1 cm) 22.92 - monotonic with the labelled drop, which is a second independent confirmation that the traced line is the pocket mouth. The render at 11.04-11.34 sits unambiguously in the 3104 bracket and cannot be confused with 3122.

THE LABEL IS WRONG AND THE DRAWING WINS - RECORD THIS SO IT DOES NOT MISLEAD A THIRD ATTEMPT. spec.json's description says "a mouth angle of 15 to 20 degrees, closer to horizontal". The drawing measures 12.0 deg from VERTICAL. The "15 to 20" is degrees from VERTICAL (adjacent to the drawing's 12, and consistent with the whole family's 8.6/11.9/12.6/22.9); the trailing gloss "closer to horizontal" is simply false. Attempt 1 failed by trusting that gloss. Equally, the task brief handed to me called this option "SLANTED" as if opposed to the drawing - the drawing shows a steeply raked, near-vertical mouth, and both readings collapse to the same number once you measure: ~12 deg off vertical, ~78 deg off horizontal.

WHY NOTHING SCORES 98. Every category except symmetry carries at least one measured deviation. The binding one is the bow (see the major finding): the overall rake is right but the mouth's upper third leaves the waistband ~6 deg too vertical. Dimensions is capped at 93 not because I found a 25% error but because I could not certify it either way - see the landmark problem below. With a Major open, the 95 waiver is not available; this is attempt 2 of 3, so budget remains.

WHAT I COULD NOT MEASURE, HONESTLY. (1) The two landmarks present in both drawing and render disagree by 22%: waistband depth gives a render/drawing scale of 0.976, belt-loop pitch gives 0.78. Every LENGTH ratio I report therefore carries roughly +/-20% - which is why the +12% mouth length is not a finding and the +25% forward offset is only a minor one. The ANGLE comparison is unaffected, being scale-free, and is cross-checked by two independent viewpoint landmarks. (2) The mouth-to-seam gap at the waistband itself is unmeasurable in the render: the leg seam fades below detectable contrast above y=277, so I compared at h=1.0-1.2 waistband depths instead of at the waistband. (3) No centimetre figure is recoverable. The drawings carry no printed scale bar, and the relation between drawn offset and labelled cm is not linear across the family (0.257 to 0.351 waistband depths per cm), so converting would be manufacturing a number. All dimensional findings are given as ratios.

SPAN AND SATURATION CHECKS PERFORMED. Three early measurements were discarded for exactly the traps in the brief: a Hough peak that locked onto the seam instead of the mouth; a tracker that ran past the mouth/seam merge and dragged the fitted angle toward vertical; and an extrapolated forward offset of 0.737 waistband depths that collapsed to 0.592 once measured directly instead of extrapolated with a global slope through a curved line. Every number reported here comes from a trace whose bounding box and per-row contrast I inspected, with the search window (+/-5 px in an 11 px corridor) verified not to be clipping the feature.
